Enter a run

Quick entries — one press fills the form; adjust anything, then Spawn the run
2 × 512 MiB ≈ 1 GiB guest RAM · vsock cids 10–11 · the full session demo — hello, welcome, echo and bye land in the transcript; the run closes itself in about ten seconds
8 × 512 MiB = 4 GiB guest RAM · 12 beats each, then the guests power themselves off — the fleet demo, about a minute
50 × 128 MiB ≈ 6.4 GiB guest RAM · 1 vCPU each · 12 beats — the validated scale scenario; the node accepts up to 64

n 1–64 · vCPUs 1–64 · memory 128 MiB and up. With beats set, each guest heartbeats that many times, then powers itself off (churn mode); the run closes itself. Empty beats runs steady, until you kill it. With a vsock CID set, each VM gets a vsock device (VM i takes CID base + i) and the agent inside talks to the orchestrator over it — the only wire a plaza guest has, there is no NIC; empty boots with no vsock at all.

Write to the serial console

The guest serves one command per heartbeat window (about 5 s); the reply lands in the transcript above. It understands: help, uname, cpu, mem, uptime, echo <text>, poweroff.

Map

live

The fleet drawn as a surveyor's plan: the machine is the plot, each run a lane, each VM a cell. A running VM's ring pulses with its serial chatter; click a cell (or walk it with the arrow keys) to open its entry.

f. 4

3D view

live

The same register, raised: the machine is the ground (gridded to its CPUs and memory), runs are platforms named on their plates, VMs are blocks whose glow follows serial chatter. The host every guest talks to stands off the plot's corner (cid 2); each session draws an arc from its VM's block to the host — from its hello line to its bye, and one beat after, so a session the register just wrote stays visible. Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, click a block to open its entry. Nothing is drawn that is not the machine, a run, a VM, the host, or a session.

The keys of the register

0Register — every run on this node
1Run — the selected entry, else the newest open run
2Machine — the node's own sheet
3Map — the fleet as a surveyor's plan
43D view — the same register, raised
5Telemetry — the session's figures, one observation per poll
?This sheet — press again, Escape, or click outside to close
fFollow new transcript lines — run and compare views
jJump to the latest line — run and compare views
tTheme — system, then light, then dark
←→↑↓Walk the VMs on the map
EnterOpen the focused VM's entry on the map · select a VM row on a run
oFrame the whole plot — on the 3D view
rFrame the selected run — on the 3D view

Keys never fire while you are typing in a field, and the canvases keep their own arrows.
